subject.title: fix(boundary-safety): guard response reads and UTF-16 truncation

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this PR's baseline-backed boundary-safety guard with its 224-entry legacy inventory as a required full and changed-check gate now?
rationale: The code is reviewable and tested, but this changes repository enforcement policy and future contributor/maintainer automation behavior; automation cannot choose the acceptable baseline size and false-positive tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt The Guard Now
options.body: Accept the 224-entry baseline as the legacy contract and merge after exact-head checks remain green or failures are proven base-owned.

options.title: Split To Guard Only
options.body: Ask for a narrower branch that drops runtime hunks already covered by current main and reviews only the guard, baseline, and guard tests.

options.title: Pause Broad Enforcement
options.body: Close or pause this PR if maintainers prefer landing focused boundary fixes without adding a broad baseline-backed check gate yet.

recommendation.title: Adopt The Guard Now
recommendation.body: Accept the 224-entry baseline as the legacy contract and merge after exact-head checks remain green or failures are proven base-owned.

likelyOwner.reason: He verified and merged the overlapping MiniMax shared-reader fix and is the strongest routing candidate for deciding whether to broaden that into a repository check gate.
